glossary.PVD: Peripheral vascular disease, narrowing of arteries outside the heart and brain, usually the legs.
glossary.diabetes mellitus: Chronic raised blood glucose from lack of insulin or resistance to it.
glossary.arterial thrombosis: Clot forming within an artery, suddenly cutting off blood supply.
glossary.superimposed infection: Infection that develops on top of an existing problem, here in dead tissue.
glossary.arterial insufficiency: Arterial blood supply too low to meet the tissue's needs.
glossary.shrivelled: Shrunken and wrinkled from drying out.
glossary.erythema: Redness of the skin from increased blood flow.
glossary.absent pulses: No palpable pulse, suggesting blocked arteries upstream.
glossary.malaise: A general feeling of being unwell.
glossary.trauma: Physical injury, even a minor cut.
glossary.systemic: Affecting the whole body rather than one area.
glossary.tissue viability: Whether tissue is still alive and can recover.
glossary.viable: Still alive and able to survive.
glossary.vascular surgery: Surgical specialty treating arteries and veins.
glossary.antiplatelet: Drug that stops platelets sticking together to form clots.
glossary.lipid control: Lowering cholesterol, usually with a statin, to slow atherosclerosis.
glossary.broad-spectrum antibiotics: Antibiotics active against many types of bacteria.
glossary.IV: Intravenous, given directly into a vein.
glossary.vancomycin: IV antibiotic for Gram-positive bacteria including MRSA.
glossary.meropenem: Very broad-spectrum carbapenem antibiotic reserved for severe infections.
glossary.ICU: Intensive care unit, for organ support in critically ill patients.
glossary.toxins: Poisons made by bacteria that damage tissue.
glossary.liquefaction: Breakdown of dead tissue into soft, fluid material.
glossary.tissue planes: Natural layers between muscles and fascia along which gas and infection spread.
glossary.systolic BP: The peak blood pressure when the heart contracts.
glossary.brachial: Relating to the upper arm; brachial pressure is measured at the arm.
glossary.X-ray: Plain radiograph; in gas gangrene it can show gas in the soft tissues.
glossary.spores: Tough dormant bacterial forms that survive in soil and enter wounds.
glossary.thrombosis: Formation of a blood clot inside a vessel.
